Marco: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — we promised a concrete action list for the streaming/chat reliability issues (timeouts, partial responses, reconnects). I'm listing owners + proposed timelines. Can folks ack or reassign?

Tasha: Ack. I'll own the reconnect/backoff change and rollout plan.

Marco: Thanks @Tasha. Primary goal: reduce client-observed partial responses and timeouts during transient GPU congestion. Proposed steps: 1) change server reconnect policy (owner: Tasha, ETA: 2026-04-05), 2) add server-side prefix cache metrics + alert (owner: Jenn, ETA: 2026-04-02), 3) add e2e harness for partial-response recovery (owner: Sam, ETA: 2026-04-09), 4) schedule canary deployment + blast-radius runbook (owner: Leo, ETA: 2026-04-06).

Jenn: I can do the metrics/dashboard and alert. Will add histograms for tail latencies and KV cache hit ratio. Putting a stub dashboard in Grafana and a pager rule for >3% partial-response rate over 5m.

Sam: For e2e I'll wire up the test harness to simulate handshake stalls and abrupt token stream cuts. Plan to add a deterministic reconnect test and a fuzz runner. Will create a test job in CI.

Tasha: Implementation note: we should prefer client-friendly reconnect semantics — exponential backoff with capped jitter and a small initial aggressive retry window for sub-second failures. Sample config I'll push to the repo:

```
reconnect:
  max_attempts: 6
  base_backoff_ms: 200
  max_backoff_ms: 5000
  jitter: true
  fast_window_ms: 1500  # quick retries allowed for immediate transient faults
```

Marco: That looks sane. Add a flag to feature-flag it per cluster so we can roll out to dedicated only first.

Tasha: Yep — will gate with `feature.streaming_reconnect_v2` and do Dedicated -> Hosted canary.

Leo (SRE): I'll take canary orchestration and the rollout runbook. Suggest steps: 1) deploy to 5% of traffic (dedicated pool), 2) monitor streaming partial-response rate, client disconnects, and token-level latency metrics, 3) rollback if error budget burn > 0.5% in 30m. ETA 2026-04-06 for runbook + playbook.

Marco: Jenn, can you add a synthetic monitor that opens 100 concurrent streaming sessions and injects 1-2 transient GPU stalls per minute? That would exercise the reconnect path and partial response conditions.

Jenn: Yep, adding a synthetic job `streaming_reconnect_smoke`. Also will add a dashboard panel that shows synthetic vs production error rates.

Sam: I'll link the e2e tests to a new Jenkins job `e2e/streaming-reconnect` and include a deterministic seed so we can repro flakes. Plan to run it nightly and on PRs touching runtime/backoff logic.

incidents-bot: Deploy job `reconnect-config-PR-482` status: CI ✅, Integration tests pending.

Tasha: I'll open the implementation PR today and tag owners. PR: https://git.redwood/reconnect/PR-482 (draft).

Marco: Ownership notes: 
- Reconnect implementation & feature flag: @Tasha (PR + QA)
- Observability + alerts + synthetic: @Jenn
- e2e/fuzz + CI: @Sam
- Canary + rollback runbook: @Leo (SRE)

Sam: One question — do we want server to return explicit reconnect hints to clients when we detect kernel preemption / queueing? We could add a header `X-Reconnect-After` or a small JSON field on stream disconnects for nicer UX.

Tasha: I like the idea. Short-term: log clear disconnect reasons for telemetry. Medium-term: proto change to include optional `reconnect_hint_ms`. Will add to the design doc.

Marco: Please capture that as an action item and keep it in the postmortem tracker.

Jenn: Putting all these into a single remediation checklist in the postmortem doc now. Link: https://docs.redwood/postmortems/chat-streaming-remediation-1951234567 (draft)

Leo (SRE): I'll coordinate a 30m rollout dry-run on 2026-04-07 at 09:00 PT with devs oncall. Can everyone confirm availability for that slot?

Tasha: Available.

Sam: Available.

Jenn: Might be tight but can join for the first 15. I'll sync offline on dashboards.

Marco: Great. One more item: recurring pattern detection — we saw spikes of partial responses on Tuesdays at 03:00 UTC for last 4 weeks. Action: add a recurring analysis job to correlate partial responses with autoscaler events and model compactions. Owner: Jenn, ETA 2026-04-12.

Jenn: noted. I'll add the correlation job using historical traces and save queries to the incident board.

Sam: For validation, I'll add an assert in the e2e that ensures at least 95% session completion across simulated transient faults. If we fall below, test fails and we block rollout.

Marco: Perfect. Can folks paste final tickets here once created? I'll close the loop after runbook + PR merge.

Tasha: PR-482 created (draft). Jira: INF-3421 for reconnect changes.

Jenn: Jira: INF-3422 (observability + synthetic). Dashboard link added to PR description.

Sam: Jira: INF-3423 (e2e + CI). Job `e2e/streaming-reconnect` created.

Leo (SRE): Runbook: INF-3424. Scheduled dry-run calendar invite sent to #incidents and oncall rotation.

Marco: Thanks team. We'll reconvene after the dry-run and one canary window. Please add brief status updates in this thread as you complete items. :thumbsup:

Tasha: Will post updates here as PRs move to review.

Sam: Posting CI link once nightly run completes.

Jenn: Dashboard + synthetic job deployed to staging. Initial synthetic shows ~0.6% partial-response when simulating 2x GPU stalls/min. Will tweak.

Leo (SRE): Canary scheduled for 2026-04-08 16:00 PT if dry-run goes well.

Marco: Closing notes: this thread will track follow-ups only. I'll mark the postmortem as updated when all INF tickets are closed. If anyone wants to add or reassign, speak up here.

Sam: quick small log snippet I found during tests: `WARN stream: client disconnected mid-token; session_id=abc123; reason=EOF` — adding to INF-3423.

Jenn: Nice catch — I'll make that a structured log field.
